profile.research_note:
New facility-phase research reusing this registrys existing Expedient operator record: operator field set from blank to Expedient based on the facility own name, directly corroborated by the companys own dedicated Milwaukee/Franklin WI facility page (MKE1, 1.6MW critical IT load).

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Expedient traces to the October 2003 acquisition of Stargate Business, a Pittsburgh-based company, after which Expedient formally designated Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania as its headquarters in May 2004, citing Stargates established infrastructure and the roughly 70 percent of Expedients workforce already based there; the company was at that time privately owned within the Continental Broadband family under Landmark Communications, and its ownership has since changed to AMP Capital, an Australian investment firm, as its investment sponsor. This registry already tracks Expedient as an existing operator record with facilities in Maryland and Pennsylvania, based on the companys own 2004 headquarters announcement and Data Center Dynamics coverage of the AMP Capital transaction.

Per the companys own site fetched this session, Expedients Milwaukee data center, designated MKE1, is located at 4777 W Ironwood in Franklin, Wisconsin, featuring 1.6 megawatts of critical IT load, a 2N UPS configuration, 3.0 megawatts of total generator capacity, 27,000 total square feet with 10,000 square feet of raised floor space, four on-net carriers, and SOC 1 and 2, HITRUST, CSF, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and CSA STAR certifications. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Expedient Milwaukee in Franklin, Wisconsin, was not individually named in the operator-level research reused here; its operator field was blank in the source data and is set here to Expedient based on the facility own name and matching address, extending the existing Expedient operator record in this registry to a third state, Wisconsin.

reading.body:
Expedient Milwaukee publishes 1.6 MW of IT capacity, making it Wisconsin's only facility with a disclosed megawatt figure, though that ranking reflects data scarcity rather than market dominance.

The facility's 27,000 square feet of technical space, with 10,000 square feet of raised floor, supports roughly 160 racks at enterprise density or 40 racks at GPU-dense training density. At either scale, 1.6 MW is small by AI infrastructure standards, where a single large training cluster absorbs tens of megawatts independently. The power envelope and technical footprint describe a campus built for enterprise workloads, not frontier AI training.

Certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, and HITRUST confirm the facility targets regulated sectors: payment processing, healthcare, and financial services. These standards require specific controls and auditability but do not indicate capability or suitability for high-density compute. The certification portfolio is orthogonal to the power and cooling constraints that bind AI scaling.

Wisconsin's dataset includes six data center facilities. Five publish no capacity figure. This single published number covers the entire state by default, making statewide capacity unknowable. For decisions about AI infrastructure placement, where gigawatts matter, 1.6 MW from one facility in one state is insufficient to assess regional opportunity or constraint.
